title: Organic Intermediates & Mechanisms (Carbocations, Carbanions, Free Radicals, & Acid-Base Analysis)
syllabus: Homolytic and heterolytic bond fission; Generation, geometry, electronic structure, and relative stabilities of reactive intermediates: carbocations (classical and non-classical, cyclopropylmethyl cation, allylic, benzylic, tropylium), carbanions, free radicals, carbenes (singlet and triplet), and nitrenes; Carbocation rearrangements: 1,2-hydride shift, 1,2-methyl/alkyl shift, ring expansion, and ring contraction; Electrophiles and nucleophiles (ambident nucleophiles, hard and soft nucleophiles); Quantitative and qualitative acidity analysis: carboxylic acids, substituted benzoic acids, phenols, alcohols, active methylene compounds; Basicity analysis: aliphatic amines (solvent, inductive, and steric effects), aromatic amines, amidines, guanidine, pyrrole vs pyridine; Nucleophilicity vs basicity; Electrophilic, nucleophilic, and radical reaction mechanisms overview

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Among the following carbocations, which one exhibits the HIGHEST thermodynamic stability in solution?
questions.solution:
The tricyclopropylmethyl carbocation, $(\text{C}_3\text{H}_5)_3\text{C}^+$, has extraordinary thermodynamic stability exceeding even the tropylium and triphenylmethyl carbocations.
1. The bent carbon-carbon $\sigma$-bonds of each cyclopropane ring ('banana bonds' with high $p$-character, $\approx sp^5$) lie in a geometry that enables exceptional, near-parallel overlap with the empty $2p$ orbital of the cationic carbon.
2. This interaction is known as bent-bond $\sigma$-conjugation (or non-classical hyperconjugative delocalization).
3. With three cyclopropyl rings, this hyper-stabilizing $\sigma$-electron donation is tripled, giving $(\text{C}_3\text{H}_5)_3\text{C}^+$ the highest stability among all given carbocations.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] When neopentyl alcohol, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, is treated with concentrated hydrochloric acid in the presence of anhydrous $\text{ZnCl}_2$, the major product obtained is:
questions.solution:
1. Protonation of the hydroxyl group followed by dehydration generates the primary neopentyl carbocation:
$$(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}_2^+ \xrightarrow{-\text{H}_2\text{O}} (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}_2 \quad (1^\circ\text{ carbocation})$$
2. The $1^\circ$ neopentyl cation undergoes a spontaneous **1,2-methyl shift** to relieve severe steric hindrance and convert into a far more stable $3^\circ$ carbocation:
$$(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}_2 \xrightarrow{1,2-\text{Me shift}} \text{CH}_3-\overset{+}{\text{C}}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \quad (3^\circ\text{ carbocation})$$
3. Attack of chloride ion ($\text{Cl}^-$) on this tertiary carbocation yields the major product:
$$\text{CH}_3-\overset{+}{\text{C}}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{Cl}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{Cl})(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$
This is 2-chloro-2-methylbutane (tert-pentyl chloride).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] Which of the following compounds exhibits the HIGHEST basicity in aqueous solution?
questions.solution:
Guanidine, $(\text{H}_2\text{N})_2\text{C}=\text{NH}$, is one of the strongest neutral organic nitrogen bases ($pK_a \approx 13.6$ for its conjugate acid):
1. Protonation occurs at the $sp^2$-hybridized imine nitrogen ($=\text{NH}$):
$$(\text{H}_2\text{N})_2\text{C}=\text{NH} + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow [(\text{H}_2\text{N})_3\text{C}]^+$$
2. The resulting guanidinium cation is stabilized by complete resonance delocalization of the positive charge symmetrically over three equivalent nitrogen atoms ($3$ identical major resonance contributors, Y-aromatic stabilization).
None of the other amines possess such symmetric conjugate acid stabilization.

questions.question:
[JEE Main 2023] The correct order of stability for the following free radicals is:
(I) $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_2$
(II) $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_2$
(III) $(\text{CH}_3)_3\dot{\text{C}}$
(IV) $(\text{CH}_3)_2\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}$
questions.solution:
Free radical stability is governed primarily by resonance delocalization followed by hyperconjugation:
1. (I) Benzyl radical ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_2$): The odd electron is delocalized over the extensive $\pi$-system of the aromatic benzene ring, producing 5 resonance structures ($4$ canonical contributors).
2. (II) Allyl radical ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_2$): The odd electron is delocalized between two equivalent terminal carbons via resonance ($2$ canonical contributors). Resonant delocalization confers higher stability than pure hyperconjugation of simple alkyl radicals.
3. (III) tert-Butyl radical ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\dot{\text{C}}$): $3^\circ$ radical with $9\ \alpha$-hydrogens participating in hyperconjugation.
4. (IV) Isopropyl radical ($(\text{CH}_3)_2\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}$): $2^\circ$ radical with only $6\ \alpha$-hydrogens.
Thus, the stability sequence is: (I) > (II) > (III) > (IV).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] Homolytic bond fission of a neutral covalent molecule leads to the generation of:
questions.solution:
In homolytic cleavage (homolysis), the covalent two-electron bond breaks symmetrically such that each of the two bonded atoms retains exactly one of the bonding electrons:
$$A-B \xrightarrow{h\nu \text{ or } \Delta} A^\bullet + B^\bullet$$
This process generates neutral, highly reactive species containing an unpaired electron, known as **free radicals**.
In contrast, heterolytic cleavage (heterolysis) involves asymmetric cleavage where one bonding atom takes both electrons, producing a pair of oppositely charged ions (cation and anion).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] The intermediate generated during the Reimer-Tiemann reaction of phenol with chloroform in the presence of aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ is:
questions.solution:
In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction:
1. The strong base ($\text{OH}^-$) deprotonates chloroform ($\text{CHCl}_3$) via an acid-base equilibrium to generate the trichloromethyl carbanion:
$$\text{CHCl}_3 + \text{OH}^- \rightleftharpoons ^-\text{CCl}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
2. The $^-\text{CCl}_3$ carbanion undergoes spontaneous $\alpha$-elimination of a chloride ion ($\text{Cl}^-$) to yield a neutral, divalent carbon intermediate with a sextet of valence electrons:
$$^-\text{CCl}_3 \xrightarrow{-\text{Cl}^-} :\text{CCl}_2 \quad (\text{Dichlorocarbene})$$
Dichlorocarbene ($:\text{CCl}_2$) is an electrophilic singlet carbene that attacks the electron-rich phenoxide ring at the ortho position.

questions.question:
[JEE Main 2021] The correct decreasing order of $pK_a$ values for the following carboxylic acids is:
(I) $\text{F}-\text{CH}_2-\text{COOH}$
(II) $\text{Cl}-\text{CH}_2-\text{COOH}$
(III) $\text{Br}-\text{CH}_2-\text{COOH}$
(IV) $\text{CH}_3-\text{COOH}$
questions.solution:
Recall that acidity is inversely related to $pK_a$:
$$\text{Higher acidity} \iff \text{Lower } pK_a$$
1. The negative inductive ($-I$) effect of halogens stabilizes the conjugate carboxylate anion ($\text{R}-\text{COO}^-$) by dispersing electron density:
$$\text{Electronegativity / } -I \text{ power: } \text{F} > \text{Cl} > \text{Br} > \text{H}$$
2. Therefore, acidic strength follows the order:
$$\text{F}-\text{CH}_2-\text{COOH} > \text{Cl}-\text{CH}_2-\text{COOH} > \text{Br}-\text{CH}_2-\text{COOH} > \text{CH}_3-\text{COOH}$$
$$\text{Acidity: } (I) > (II) > (III) > (IV)$$
3. Inverting for $pK_a$ values:
$$pK_a: (IV) > (III) > (II) > (I)$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Which of the following carbanions is the LEAST stable?
questions.solution:
Carbanions possess an unshared electron pair on a negatively charged carbon atom (an electron-rich intermediate):
1. Electron-donating groups ($+I$ inductive effect) pump electron density into the already electron-rich center, increasing charge concentration and destabilizing the carbanion.
2. In the tert-butyl carbanion, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}^-$, there are three methyl groups exerting additive $+I$ effects directed toward the negative carbon.
3. The stability order of simple alkyl carbanions is strictly inverted relative to carbocations:
$$\text{Methyl} > 1^\circ > 2^\circ > 3^\circ$$
$$\text{CH}_3^- > \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2^- > (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}^- > (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}^-$$
Hence, the tertiary butyl carbanion is the least stable.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] When cyclobutylmethyl carbocation undergoes rearrangement, the primary driving force is:
options: Ring expansion to a five-membered cyclopentyl cation to relieve Baeyer ring strain
Hydride shift to retain the four-membered ring
Loss of a proton to form an allene
questions.solution:
1. In the cyclobutylmethyl carbocation ($c\text{-C}_4\text{H}_7-\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}_2$), a $1^\circ$ carbocation is situated directly adjacent to a strained four-membered cyclobutane ring.
2. The internal bond angles of the cyclobutane ring are compressed to $\approx 88-90^\circ$, causing substantial angle strain (Baeyer strain $\approx 110\text{ kJ/mol}$).
3. A $\sigma$-bond of the ring migrates (ring expansion) onto the exocyclic cationic carbon:
$$\text{Cyclobutylmethyl cation} \xrightarrow{\text{ring expansion}} \text{Cyclopentyl cation}$$
4. Ring expansion from a 4-membered to a 5-membered ring relaxes the bond angles to $\approx 108^\circ$, relieving ring strain and converting a less stable $1^\circ$ carbocation into a more stable secondary cyclopentyl carbocation.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] The geometry and electronic structure of a singlet carbene ($:\text{CH}_2$) are:
options: $sp^2$ hybridized, bent geometry with paired electrons in an $sp^2$ orbital and an empty $p$-orbital
$sp$ hybridized, linear geometry with two unpaired electrons in degenerate $p$-orbitals
$sp^3$ hybridized, tetrahedral geometry with two lone pairs
$sp^2$ hybridized, planar geometry with two unpaired electrons with parallel spins
questions.solution:
Carbenes ($:\text{CR}_2$) exist in two distinct electronic states:
1. **Singlet carbene:**
- The carbon atom is $sp^2$ hybridized, adopting a bent (angular) geometry.
- The two non-bonding electrons are spin-paired in an $sp^2$ hybrid orbital, while the unhybridized $2p$ orbital remains vacant.
- Total spin $S = 0$, spin multiplicity $= 2S + 1 = 1$ (singlet), diamagnetic.
2. **Triplet carbene:**
- The carbon atom is $sp$ hybridized (linear or quasi-linear with $sp^2$ bend).
- The two non-bonding electrons occupy two separate degenerate orbitals with parallel spins ($S = 1$, multiplicity $= 3$, paramagnetic).
Thus, the singlet carbene is $sp^2$ hybridized, bent, with paired electrons in an $sp^2$ orbital and an empty $p$-orbital.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] Which of the following represents an AMBIDENT nucleophile?
questions.solution:
An ambident nucleophile is an anionic or neutral nucleophilic species possessing two distinct nucleophilic donor atoms with unshared electron pairs through either of which it can launch a nucleophilic attack:
1. Cyanide ion ($[:\text{C}\equiv\text{N}:]^-$): Can attack through its carbon atom (forming nitriles/cyanides, $\text{R}-\text{CN}$) or through its nitrogen atom (forming isonitriles/isocyanides, $\text{R}-\text{NC}$).
2. Another classic example is the nitrite ion ($[:\text{O}-\text{N}=\text{O}]^-$), which can attack through oxygen (alkyl nitrites, $\text{R}-\text{ONO}$) or nitrogen (nitroalkanes, $\text{R}-\text{NO}_2$).
Hydroxide, methoxide, and ammonia possess only one type of nucleophilic donor site.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds has the MOST acidic hydrogen (lowest $pK_a$)?
questions.solution:
Acidity of active methylene compounds ($-\text{CH}_2-$ sandwiched between two electron-withdrawing groups) depends on the magnitude of resonance stabilization of the resulting carbanion:
1. In pentane-2,4-dione (acetylacetone, $\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_3$), deprotonation generates a carbanion whose negative charge is strongly delocalized onto two highly electronegative ketone oxygen atoms ($pK_a \approx 9$).
2. In diethyl malonate, the ester oxygens donate electron density by cross-conjugation ($-\ddot{\text{O}}-\text{Et}$), which diminishes the electron-withdrawing power of the ester carbonyls, making its active methylene protons less acidic ($pK_a \approx 13$).
3. Monocarbonyls (acetaldehyde $pK_a \approx 17$, acetone $pK_a \approx 20$) are significantly less acidic than $\beta$-dicarbonyls.
Therefore, pentane-2,4-dione has the most acidic hydrogen.

questions.question:
[JEE Main 2023] In the following reaction:
$$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{OH})-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2 \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+, \Delta} \text{Major Alkene}$$
The major product formed and the rearrangement involved are:
questions.solution:
1. Protonation of the alcohol followed by loss of water yields a secondary carbocation:
$$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{OH})-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2 \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} \text{CH}_3-\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2 \quad (2^\circ\text{ carbocation, } 4\ \alpha\text{-H})$$
2. The adjacent carbon C-3 is tertiary. A **1,2-hydride shift** occurs rapidly:
$$\text{CH}_3-\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2 \xrightarrow{1,2-\text{H}^- \text{ shift}} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\overset{+}{\text{C}}(\text{CH}_3)_2 \quad (3^\circ\text{ carbocation, } 7\ \alpha\text{-H})$$
3. Loss of a proton from C-2 according to Zaitsev's rule yields the most substituted, most stable alkene:
$$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\overset{+}{\text{C}}(\text{CH}_3)_2 \xrightarrow{-\text{H}^+} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_2$$
This is 2-methylbut-2-ene formed via a 1,2-hydride shift.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] Why is pyrrole substantially WEAKER as a base than pyridine?
options: The lone pair of electrons on nitrogen in pyrrole forms part of the aromatic $6\ \pi$-electron sextet and is not readily available for protonation
Pyrrole is an aliphatic secondary amine
The conjugate acid of pyrrole is resonance stabilized
Pyridine has a localized positive charge on carbon
questions.solution:
1. In **pyrrole** ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_5\text{N}$), the nitrogen atom is $sp^2$ hybridized and its lone pair resides in an unhybridized $p$-orbital that participates in the cyclic aromatic $\pi$-system ($4\ \pi$-electrons from double bonds $+ 2\ \pi$-electrons from $\text{N}$ lone pair $= 6\ \pi$-electron aromatic sextet). Protonating this lone pair disrupts aromaticity, which is energetically unfavorable ($pK_a$ of conjugate acid $\approx 0.4$, extremely weak base).
2. In **pyridine** ($\text{C}_5\text{H}_5\text{N}$), the nitrogen atom is $sp^2$ hybridized and forms one double bond within the ring. Its lone pair occupies an $sp^2$ hybrid orbital that lies in the plane of the ring, orthogonal to the $\pi$-system. The lone pair does not contribute to the aromatic sextet and remains available for proton donation ($pK_a$ of conjugate acid $\approx 5.25$).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] Which of the following carbocations will NOT undergo rearrangement?
questions.solution:
Carbocations undergo rearrangement only if the rearrangement leads to a thermodynamically more stable species:
1. In $(\text{CH}_3)_3\overset{+}{\text{C}}$ (tert-butyl cation), the carbocation is tertiary with $9\ \alpha$-hydrogens. Any 1,2-hydride or 1,2-methyl shift would generate a less stable primary carbocation ($1^\circ$). Therefore, it is at an energy minimum and will not rearrange.
2. In $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}_2$ ($1^\circ$), a 1,2-hydride shift yields a more stable $2^\circ$ carbocation ($\text{CH}_3-\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}-\text{CH}_3$).
3. In $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}-\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}_2$ ($1^\circ$), a 1,2-hydride shift yields the tertiary carbocation $(\text{CH}_3)_3\overset{+}{\text{C}}$.
4. In $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}-\text{CH}_3$ ($2^\circ$), a 1,2-methyl shift yields a stable tertiary carbocation.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] The correct order of nucleophilicity of halide ions in a POLAR PROTIC solvent (such as water or ethanol) is:
questions.solution:
In a **polar protic solvent** (like $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ or $\text{ROH}$):
1. The solvent molecules engage in strong hydrogen bonding with anions.
2. Small ions with high charge density (like $\text{F}^-$) are tightly encased in a rigid, thick hydration shell that suppresses nucleophilic attack.
3. The large iodide ion ($\text{I}^-$) has low charge density, weak solvation, and high polarizability. Its outer electron cloud readily distorts toward an electrophilic center.
Therefore, nucleophilicity in polar protic solvents follows the order:
$$\text{I}^- > \text{Br}^- > \text{Cl}^- > \text{F}^-$$
(In polar aprotic solvents like DMSO or acetone, where hydrogen bonding is absent, the order inverts to $\text{F}^- > \text{Cl}^- > \text{Br}^- > \text{I}^-$).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Which of the following species acts as an electrophile?
questions.solution:
An electrophile is an electron-deficient species that can accept an electron pair from an electron-rich donor:
1. $\text{BF}_3$ (boron trifluoride): The central boron atom is $sp^2$ hybridized with only $6$ valence electrons (an incomplete octet). It has a vacant unhybridized $2p$ orbital that readily accepts an electron pair, acting as an electrophile (Lewis acid).
2. $\text{NH}_3$, $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, and $\text{CH}_3\text{O}^-$ possess lone pairs of electrons and act as nucleophiles/bases.

questions.question: The hyperconjugation effect (Baker-Nathan effect) in alkyl-substituted carbocations involves the overlap between:
options: $\sigma(\text{C}-\text{H})$ orbital and the vacant $2p$ orbital of the cationic carbon
questions.solution:
Hyperconjugation in carbocations is a $\sigma-\pi$ (or $\sigma-p$) delocalization phenomenon:
1. The adjacent $\alpha$-carbon has $\text{C}-\text{H}$ $\sigma$-bonds.
2. The electron pair in the $\sigma(\text{C}-\text{H})$ bonding orbital overlaps with the adjacent, coplanar empty unhybridized $2p$ orbital of the positively charged $sp^2$ carbon.
3. This overlap disperses the positive charge onto the hydrogen atoms, providing stabilization without requiring formal bond formation (no-bond resonance).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] In the free radical chlorination of methane, the chain-propagating steps are:
questions.solution:
The mechanism of photochemical chlorination of methane consists of:
1. **Initiation:** $\text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{h\nu} 2\text{Cl}^\bullet$
2. **Propagation:**
- Step 1: $\text{Cl}^\bullet + \text{CH}_4 \rightarrow \text{HCl} + \dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_3$
- Step 2: $\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_3 + \text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{Cl} + \text{Cl}^\bullet$
(These two steps continuously consume reactants and regenerate the chlorine radical).
3. **Termination:** Radical recombination steps like $2\text{Cl}^\bullet \rightarrow \text{Cl}_2$, $\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_3 + \text{Cl}^\bullet \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$, and $2\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_3 \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_6$.
Thus, Option A correctly represents the propagation steps.

questions.question:
[JEE Main 2020] The correct order of basicity among the following anilines is:
(I) Aniline
(II) 4-Nitroaniline
(III) 4-Methoxyaniline (p-anisidine)
(IV) 4-Chloroaniline
questions.solution:
Basicity of anilines depends on the availability of the nitrogen lone pair for protonation:
- Electron-donating groups ($+M, +I$) increase electron density on $-\text{NH}_2$, enhancing basicity.
- Electron-withdrawing groups ($-M, -I$) pull electron density away, decreasing basicity.
1. (III) 4-Methoxyaniline (p-anisidine): The para methoxy group ($-\text{OCH}_3$) donates electron density into the ring through a strong $+M$ effect, increasing electron density on nitrogen and making it the strongest base.
2. (I) Aniline: Unsubstituted baseline.
3. (IV) 4-Chloroaniline: The chloro group has an electron-withdrawing $-I$ effect that outweighs its weak $+M$ back-donation, reducing basicity relative to aniline.
4. (II) 4-Nitroaniline: The para nitro group ($-\text{NO}_2$) exerts powerful $-M$ and $-I$ effects, delocalizing the nitrogen lone pair directly into the nitro oxygens, drastically decreasing basicity ($pK_b \approx 13$).
Hence, the basicity order is: (III) > (I) > (IV) > (II).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Calculate the total number of hyperconjugative hydrogens ($\alpha$-hydrogens) in the 2,3-dimethylbut-2-yl cation, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}^+-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$.
questions.solution:
Examine the structure of $(\text{CH}_3)_2\overset{+}{\text{C}}-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$:
- The positively charged carbon is bonded to:
  - Two methyl groups ($2 \times -\text{CH}_3$), which contribute $2 \times 3 = 6\ \alpha$-hydrogens.
  - One isopropyl carbon ($-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$), which contributes $1\ \alpha$-hydrogen.
$$\text{Total } \alpha\text{-hydrogens} = 6 + 1 = 7.0$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] In the solvolysis of 1-bromo-2,2-dimethylpropane in ethanol under heating, how many methyl groups undergo a 1,2-shift during the carbocation rearrangement step?
questions.solution:
1. Heterolysis of the $\text{C}-\text{Br}$ bond yields the primary neopentyl carbocation:
$$(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{Br} \xrightarrow{-\text{Br}^-} (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}_2$$
2. To achieve stability, exactly **one** of the three methyl groups migrates with its bonding pair of electrons as a methide ion ($:\text{CH}_3^-$) from C-2 to the adjacent C-1 (a 1,2-methyl shift):
$$(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}_2 \xrightarrow{1,2-\text{methyl shift}} \text{CH}_3-\overset{+}{\text{C}}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$
Thus, exactly $1.0$ methyl group shifts.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] Find the total number of canonical resonance structures possible for the tropylium cation ($\text{C}_7\text{H}_7^+$).
questions.solution:
The tropylium ion is a regular, planar, seven-membered ring with complete cyclic conjugation containing $6\ \pi$-electrons:
- The single positive charge can be placed sequentially at each of the seven carbon atoms around the symmetrical ring without altering the overall bonding pattern.
- Each arrangement generates an equivalent canonical contributing structure.
Therefore, there are exactly $7.0$ equivalent canonical resonance contributors.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Among the following chemical species: $\text{AlCl}_3, \text{BF}_3, \text{H}_3\text{O}^+, \text{SO}_3, \text{NH}_4^+, \text{NO}_2^+, :\text{CCl}_2, \text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$, how many can act as ELECTROPHILES in organic reactions?
questions.solution:
Identify electrophilic species (capable of accepting an electron pair into a low-lying vacant orbital or polarizable center):
1. $\text{AlCl}_3$: Incomplete octet (6 valence electrons), vacant $3p/3d$ orbital $\implies$ Electrophile
2. $\text{BF}_3$: Incomplete octet (6 valence electrons), vacant $2p$ orbital $\implies$ Electrophile
3. $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$: Complete octet, acts as a proton donor; the ion itself does not accept an electron pair $\implies$ Not an electrophile
4. $\text{SO}_3$: Strongly polar $\text{S}=\text{O}$ bonds with empty $d$-orbitals on sulfur, attacks aromatic rings in sulfonation $\implies$ Electrophile
5. $\text{NH}_4^+$: Complete octet, no vacant orbital $\implies$ Not an electrophile
6. $\text{NO}_2^+$: Nitronium ion, positively charged linear electrophile in aromatic nitration $\implies$ Electrophile
7. $:\text{CCl}_2$: Dichlorocarbene, 6 valence electrons, vacant $p$-orbital $\implies$ Electrophile
8. $\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$: Grignard reagent, carbon acts as a nucleophile/carbanion $\implies$ Nucleophile
Total electrophiles $= 5.0$ ($\text{AlCl}_3, \text{BF}_3, \text{SO}_3, \text{NO}_2^+, :\text{CCl}_2$).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] Calculate the total number of valence electrons present on the carbon atom of a free methyl radical ($\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_3$).
questions.solution:
In a methyl radical ($\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_3$):
- The central carbon forms three single $\text{C}-\text{H}$ covalent bonds, contributing $3 \times 2 = 6$ shared electrons.
- It also possesses one unshared, non-bonding unpaired electron.
$$\text{Total valence electrons} = 6 + 1 = 7.0$$
